title: Build wrapper rejects its documented Release positional argument
body: The required queued baseline invocation ./build-wsl.sh Release --target ... exited 2 before compilation because the wrapper rejected Release, even though its own usage documents Release as accepted. Recovery used the wrapper without Release. Make the documented invocation and parser agree so every lane can use the supported Release path.

title: Build wrapper does not reliably dispatch repeated target arguments
body: The queued baseline command supplied four repeated --target arguments, but the wrapper/CMake path only built the first requested target. Recovery required separate queued cmake --build build/wsl --target commands for the remaining targets. Make multi-target selection explicit and fail loudly or dispatch every target.

title: Header-only CPU mirrors need a declarative CTest classification
body: The exposure mirror was a pure CPU header-table test, but its RenderGraph link closure classified it as GPU and disabled it under the translated Release CTest configuration. To witness it in the CPU partition after assert conversion, the test had to drop the facade link and manually reproduce include directories (RenderGraph include, Core, Vulkan, generated, Vulkan SDK, GLM). Add a declarative CPU-only classification or header-only dependency surface so tests do not hand-wire classifier workarounds.

title: CPU CTest must materialize all registered targets before a full Release witness
body: The first full CPU Release CTest saw seven missing executables and a missing asset MANIFEST; I had to run the queued full cmake --build build/wsl before the retry. Suggested consolidation: make the full CPU gate own target and asset materialization or refuse stale partial trees with a clear preflight.
